CapCut vs VEXI: Video Editor or Social Media in One App?
CapCut and VEXI, side by side: what each one does and what it costs, from each company's own pages.
CapCut gives you a full set of editing and design tools [1]. Here is how it compares with one app that does the edit, the post and the posting for you.

CapCut is a photo and video editor for phone, desktop and the web [1]. On its timeline you trim and split clips and add music, transitions, effects and auto-captions [3]. It also has AI video and image generation and an AI design tool for ads, banners and branded content [1][4]. There is a no-cost plan; Pro is USD 19.99 a month billed monthly, or USD 179.99 a year [2]. As an editor, it is very good.

VEXI is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

The difference is who does the editing. CapCut is built for people who like to edit, with AI helpers such as EditPilot that turn your direction into edits on the timeline [1]. VEXI does the edit when you ask, writes the caption, and posts it. VEXI costs more than CapCut: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month [2]. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
CapCut gives you a timeline editor: you trim and split clips and add music, effects and captions, with AI tools to help [3].
VEXI edits the video for you: cuts, B-roll, music and captions. How deep the edit goes depends on your plan's mode, and anything you ask for wins.
CapCut's own guide says you can share a finished video straight to TikTok, and it walks through scheduling with TikTok's website or a separate tool [5].
VEXI schedules and posts to your connected accounts itself.

One app: you ask, and it writes, designs, edits the video and posts it. Autopilot runs your week ahead.
What does CapCut do for social media?

CapCut covers the edit and the design, with AI tools to help [1]. Its own guide says you can share a finished video straight to TikTok, and it points to TikTok's website or a separate tool for scheduling [5]. VEXI also writes the caption, plans the week and posts to your connected accounts.
For most posts, yes: VEXI edits the video for you with cuts, B-roll, music and captions, then posts it. If you love editing by hand, CapCut's timeline editor is built for that [3].

CapCut has a no-cost plan [2]. Pro is USD 19.99 a month billed monthly, or USD 179.99 a year [2]. Its pricing page says the prices shown are for reference only, and that plans can vary by region, platform and current offer [2].
